youtube_title: You Signed the Gym Waiver. In New York, That May Not Protect the Gym 🦝⚖️
caption: New York General Obligations Law 5-326 voids waivers at paid recreational facilities that try to excuse the operator's own negligence. Injury alone isn't negligence, and not every program is covered.
script: That gym waiver you signed might be worth nothing in New York. [disclaimer] New York's General Obligations Law has a section aimed at a specific kind of fine print. If you pay to use a pool, a gym, an amusement park, or a similar recreational place, any agreement that exempts the owner or operator from liability for its own negligence, or its employees' negligence, is void as against public policy and wholly unenforceable. So picture a hypothetical. You pay for a gym membership and sign a waiver saying the gym isn't responsible for anything. Then you get hurt because staff ignored a broken machine. Under this law, that waiver can't shield the gym from your negligence claim. But this is where the internet oversells it. First, the law covers certain paid recreational facilities. Not every sports release or instructional program falls under it. Second, getting hurt doesn't prove negligence. You still have to show the gym was careless, and that the carelessness caused the injury. Third, the gym can still argue you accepted the normal risks of the activity. So the waiver isn't magic, but neither is the statute. [loop] So the next time you sign a stack of gym paperwork, remember
